The analog block is a HARD macro (pre-hardened GDS+LEF). OpenLane consumes it as a black-box
placed instance; it never pushes logic inside the analog ring (real SG13G2 gates stay opaque).
OpenLane expects macros as LEF class CORE with pins. The consolidated gate ring proof gave the
real measured osc period the SDC derives its create_clock from.
Tell OpenLane the ring oscillator output is a real (measured) clock domain, so the digital
flow treats out/outb as a 200 MHz-ish source of truth rather than unconstrined comb init.
Keep the emitter's own timing lane: the SDC create_clock at src/sdc/timing.sdc uses the
period echoed by the consolidated emitter's ngspice .meas proof (osc_period/osc_freq rows).
OpenLane macro placement: put the hardened ring flush against the analog pins it drives.
